name: Multi-Turn Session
description: A long, tool-free iterative feature session: a developer hones a health-check endpoint across six turns. The system prompt is byte-stable across every turn and the conversation history grows monotonically, so the request prefix is stable and the tail churns — the shape L0 prefix caching and history-aging compression target. No tool calls; pure chat traffic.

expect.intent: exercise L0 prefix stability on a growing pure-chat history and history-aging on old turns

async function probeReady(pool, ms) { const timer = new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r(false), ms)); const ok = pool.query("SELECT 1").then(() => true); return (await Promise.race([timer, ok])) === true; } app.get("/readyz", async (req, res) => { const ready = await probeReady(pool, 2000); res.status(ready ? 200 : 503).json({ status: ready ? // src/readyProbe.js
export async function probeReady(pool, ms) { const timer = new Promise((r) => setTimeout(() => r({ ok: false, reason: "timeout" }), ms)); const ok = pool.query("SELECT 1").then(() => ({ ok: true })).catch((e) => ({ ok: false, reason: e.message })); return Promise.race([timer, ok]); } // route: app.get("/readyz", async (req, res) => { const r = await probeReady(pool, 2000); res.status(r.ok ? 200 : 503).json({ status: r.ok ? "ok" : "unavailable", reason: r.reason }); });
One more refinement: when the probe fails, include the latency in milliseconds in the response body so ops can see how slow the check was. Keep the timeout at 2 seconds.
